A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and rendered figures and equations support comparison. Much of v1's Appendices A–C reappears as Appendices B–D in v2.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical results, proofs and mathematical examples, without original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its new plots and numerical matrix example illustrate analytical calculations rather than experimental or simulation outcomes.

M1.justification: The reward-learning and regularized/unregularized policy-optimization procedures are unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the safety-matrix construction already derived in v1 Appendix B.3.1–B.3.2 as explicit pseudocode.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or tasks actually used for training or empirical evaluation. The new chatbot and toy-MDP examples are mathematical illustrations; 'mixed bandit' becomes 'contextual bandit' without changing the underlying framework.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods. The expanded citations and discussion of other algorithms do not constitute added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols are introduced or revised. The MSE extension and numerical toy-MDP parameters concern mathematical analyses rather than reported training or evaluation runs.

E4.justification: v2 adds analytical case studies: Appendix B.4 examines chatbot regret as harmful-query frequency and damage vary, while Appendix C.3.4 demonstrates safety constraints and redundancy in a toy MDP. These supplement the general theory without adding empirical ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 add concrete analytical results, including harm-dependent safety-threshold curves and a four-row safety matrix for rewards (2.78, 1.98, 1.6), discount 0.4, regret threshold 0.8 and error tolerance 0.2. These are new worked calculations, not measured performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds MSE safety definitions and transfer arguments (Appendix B.3), conditions making every distribution unsafe (Corollary 3.4/C.6), and Proposition C.7's compatibility proof. It also revises face-dimension reasoning in v1 Proposition B.20/v2 Proposition C.22. The new RLHF Definition C.27 contains an apparent repeated-action indexing error; the underlying preference-KL results already appeared in v1.

C1.justification: The central warning about reward error, regret and regularization is retained. v2 adds the explicit claim that some MDPs admit no safe distribution at fixed tolerances and corrects the discussion's regularized asymptotic guarantee to a bound based on reference-policy regret.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's broad infinite-data convergence expectation with an explicit explanation that reward non-identifiability can prevent Equation (1) even with infinite data, and distinguishes assumed accuracy from PAC sample-complexity guarantees. It also develops the chatbot harm interpretation, qualifies MSE generalization, and discusses computational redundancy and limitations of constructing the safety matrix.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 newly specifies candidate enumeration, rank and cone-membership checks, and matrix assembly; the accompanying text identifies exponential runtime. Figure 4 supplies numerical construction inputs. v1 provided the algebraic construction without this procedural documentation.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning against offline-RL and contextual-bandit theory, including Song et al. (2024), Foster et al. (2021), and Uehara and Sun (2021). v2 distinguishes its adversarial error-to-regret guarantees from sample-complexity and coverage results much more explicitly.

P1.justification: The introduction, problem formalization, related work and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. v2 explains safety before unsafety, adds explanatory appendix subsections, reorganizes the appendix around extended related work, and consistently replaces 'mixed bandit' with 'contextual bandit'.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, and the retained Figure 1 is resized and relocated. v2 adds the pipeline diagram, analytical threshold plot, numerical safety-region visualization and Algorithm 1 display, substantially changing the document's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision and accessibility by correcting the regularized-limit summary, clarifying identifiability and PAC scope, and making the existing matrix construction explicit through Algorithm 1 and Figure 4. The MSE extension and expanded literature comparisons are useful, while most central results were already established in v1. New notation slips, notably Definition C.27's repeated action argument, temper the precision gains.
